A: Axial T2-weighted MRI demonstrates a left orbital lesion extending toward the orbital apex with associated cavernous sinus involvement, attributed in the article to idiopathic orbital inflammatory pseudotumor within the spectrum of Tolosa-Hunt syndrome. B: Pre-contrast axial MRI panel shows the orbital lesion and its cavernous sinus extension in a patient whose findings were interpreted as idiopathic orbital inflammatory pseudotumor, falling within the Tolosa-Hunt syndrome spectrum. C: Post-contrast axial MRI clearly demonstrates a homogeneously enhancing left orbital lesion with cavernous sinus extension, matching the reported Tolosa-Hunt syndrome-spectrum inflammatory process. D: Coronal post-contrast MRI shows the enhancing left orbital lesion, specifically supporting orbital apex disease in the reported Tolosa-Hunt syndrome case.

T2 weighted Brain MRI axial sequence demonstrating a T2 hypointense lesion (white arrow) centered in the mid- to posterior intraconal compartment of the left orbit involving the intraocular muscles near the region of the orbital apex. (A) The lesion is seen compressing the optic nerve sheath displacing it superomedially. Similar signal intensity is observed within the left cavernous sinus consistent with sinus invasion (orange arrow). Axial (B) pre- and (C) post-contrast T1 weighted sequences demonstrating homogeneous enhancement of the orbital lesion (green arrow) with associated proptosis and extension to the cavernous sinus (yellow arrow). (D) Coronal post-contrast T1 weighted MR sequence demonstrating homogeneous enhancement of the orbital lesion (pink arrow).
in_text_mentions: An MRI scan of the orbits, both with and without contrast, was performed using a Philips Achieva model scanner with a 1.5-tesla magnet. The MRI revealed a homogeneously enhancing lesion in the posterior intraconal compartment of the left orbit, extending to the orbital apex and involving the adjacent extraocular muscles (Figure 1). Given the clinical findings described above, these results were most consistent with idiopathic orbital inflammatory pseudotumor, falling within the spectrum of THS, versus lymphoma.
